title: Jellyfish
objective: After this level you can describe jellyfish and how they sting.
summary: A jellyfish is about 95 percent water, with no brain, heart or blood: a nerve net and one opening do the job. It stings with nematocysts, harpoons that fire in about 700 nanoseconds.

cards.headline: A jellyfish is about 95 percent water.
cards.body: No brain. No heart. Not even blood. It's close to a bag of seawater with a plan. So how does something that simple catch its dinner?

cards.headline: Simple, not sloppy
cards.body: A jellyfish senses its world with a nerve net, a simple web of nerves instead of a brain. Its gut is just as minimal: one cavity works as both stomach and intestine, and a single opening serves as both mouth and anus. Everything goes in and out the same door. Economical, if not elegant.

cards.headline: Harpoons on a hair trigger
cards.body: The hunting happens in stinging capsules called nematocysts. Each holds a tiny harpoon, coiled up and waiting. Trigger them and hundreds fire at once. Each jab lasts about 700 nanoseconds and hits hard enough to pierce a crustacean's shell. That's how an animal without a brain gets through armor.

cards.fact: No brain, no heart, still an animal.
cards.context: Run a jellyfish through Level 1's checklist. Many cells, no cell walls: check. Eats other living things: check, caught with harpoons. Level 1 put jellyfish on the animal map for exactly these reasons. The checklist never asked for a brain, a heart or blood.

questions.prompt: What does a jellyfish use instead of a brain?

options.label: Its stomach
options.rationale: The gut digests; the nerve net senses.

questions.explanation: Jellyfish sense and respond to their surroundings with a simple nerve net.
